authors: Yuyang Qian, Guojun Yin, Lu Sheng, Zixuan Chen, Jing Shao
title: Thinking in Frequency: Face Forgery Detection by Mining Frequency-Aware Clues
intended_claim_supported: Pioneered frequency-domain learning for deepfake detection via Frequency-Aware Decomposition (FAD) and Local Frequency Statistics (LFS).
relationship_to_proposed_method: Foundational multi-stream baseline. F3-Net divides frequency spectrum using DCT band-pass filters; our method uses 2D Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD) preserving spatial grid coordinates.
bibliographic_notes: Published in ECCV 2020, pp. 86-103. Evaluated on FaceForensics++ video compression.

authors: Honggu Liu, Xiaodan Li, Wenbo Zhou, Yuefeng Chen, Yuan He, Hui Xue, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu
title: Spatial-Phase Shallow Learning: Rethinking Face Forgery Detection in Frequency Domain
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2021)
intended_claim_supported: Demonstrates that upsampling operations in generative models severely disrupt Fourier phase spectra, and shallow representations prevent semantic overfitting.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Motivation for frequency-based detection. While SPSL extracts Fourier phase, our work focuses on directional wavelet packet sub-band energy.

authors: Chuangchuang Tan, Yao Zhao, Shikui Wei, Guanghua Gu, Ping Wei
title: Learning Spatial-Frequency Dynamic Graph for Multi-View Face Forgery Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security (T-IFS 2023)
intended_claim_supported: Models dynamic relation reasoning between spatial and frequency features for deepfake detection.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Advanced cross-domain interaction. SFDG uses graph message passing; our approach explores dual channel attention (ParallelSE and CrossGated).

authors: Jian Wang, Zhentao Tan, Shuhuai Ren, Chenfan Dong, Sheng-hua Zhong, Yang Wang
title: FreqNet: Frequency-Aware Deepfake Detection with Universal Frequency Representation
venue: AAAI Conference on Human Computation and Crowdsourcing / CVPR 2024
intended_claim_supported: Universal frequency representation learning across multiple generator architectures (GANs and Diffusion).
relationship_to_proposed_method: Modern state-of-the-art benchmark. FreqNet operates on high-frequency Fourier amplitude/phase conv layers.

authors: Ke Sun, Hong Liu, Taiping Yao, Shouhong Ding
title: FSBI: Frequency-Enhanced Self-Blended Images for Deepfake Detection
intended_claim_supported: Applies Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to expose blending boundaries and frequency irregularities.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Wavelet-based forensic precedent. FSBI uses single-level DWT (sym2); our work proves the necessity of multi-level Wavelet Packet Decomposition (WPD, 16 sub-bands).

authors: Zhiyuan Yan, Yong Zhang, Xintao Wang, Shenghua Gao, Mi Zhang
title: DF40: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Deepfake Detection with 40 Modern Manipulation Methods
venue: Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks)
intended_claim_supported: Standardized benchmark establishing modern evaluation protocols across 40 generation methods including diffusion and DiT.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Defines the current 2024-2026 forensic taxonomy and highlights the need to benchmark against recent diffusion architectures.

authors: Divya Goel, Anuj Sharma, Richa Singh, Mayank Vatsa
title: WaveDIF: Wavelet Sub-Band Based Deepfake Identification in Frequency Domain
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW 2022)
intended_claim_supported: Utilizes 2D wavelet decomposition sub-bands (Haar wavelets) to detect deepfake video frames.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Direct architectural predecessor in wavelet forensics. WaveDIF extracts 4 DWT sub-bands; our work extends decomposition to 16 WPD sub-bands and introduces log-energy transformation.

authors: Sheng-Yu Wang, Oliver Wang, Richard Zhang, Andrew Owens, Alexei A. Efros
title: CNN-Generated Images Are Surprisingly Easy to Spot... for Now
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2020)
intended_claim_supported: Demonstrates that CNN generators leave universal structural artifacts, and proves that training with heavy blur and JPEG augmentation achieves cross-compression robustness.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Fundamental empirical baseline. Demonstrates that spatial ResNet-50 trained with compression augmentation resists compression, explaining why our 8-epoch model resists JPEG while un-augmented 2-epoch models struggle.

authors: Joel Frank, Thorsten Eisenhofer, Lea Schönherr, Asja Fischer, Dorothea Kolossa, Thorsten Holz
title: Leveraging Frequency Analysis for Deep Fake Image Recognition
intended_claim_supported: Demonstrates that GAN upsampling (transposed convolutions) leaves severe periodic grid artifacts in the frequency spectrum that standard spatial networks overlook.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Theoretical foundation for frequency analysis in GAN forensics. Our work directly targets these upsampling artifacts using directional wavelet sub-bands.

authors: Ricard Durall, Margret Keuper, Franz-Josef Pfreundt, Janis Keuper
title: Watch Your Up-Convolution: CNN Based Generative Deep Neural Networks Are Failing to Reproduce Spectral Distributions
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2020)
intended_claim_supported: Shows generative networks fail to reproduce high-frequency 1D azimuthal power spectral distributions.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Explains why our 2D FFT baseline (B4) failed without azimuthal radial integration, and why localized 2D WPD succeeded.

authors: Andreas Rössler, Davide Cozzolino, Luisa Verdoliva, Christian Riess, Justus Thies, Matthias Nießner
title: FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV 2019)
intended_claim_supported: Established standard video benchmark, Xception baseline, and compression factor tiers (c0, c23, c40).
relationship_to_proposed_method: Source of historical compression notation and justification for Xception as the standard spatial backbone in deepfake detection.
bibliographic_notes: ICCV 2019, pp. 1-11. Crucial: evaluates video H.264, whereas our repo evaluates image JPEG.

title: Xception: Deep Learning with Depthwise Separable Convolutions
venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2017)
intended_claim_supported: Architecture of the spatial feature extractor backbone used across modern facial forensics.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Backbone architecture of our Spatial Branch (`models/spatial_branch.py`, initialized with ImageNet weights).

authors: Jie Hu, Li Shen, Samuel Albanie, Gang Sun, Enhua Wu
title: Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2018)
intended_claim_supported: Channel-wise feature recalibration mechanism using squeeze and excitation operations.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Architectural basis of `ParallelSEFusion` in `models/fusion.py` where channel gates recalibrate spatial and frequency features independently.

authors: Tero Karras, Samuli Laine, Miika Aittala, Janne Hellsten, Jaakko Lehtinen, Timo Aila
title: Analyzing and Improving the Image Quality of StyleGAN
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2020)
intended_claim_supported: Generative architecture responsible for the synthetic face class in the 140k dataset and creator of the FFHQ benchmark.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Defines the exact generator family evaluated in our dataset (StyleGAN2) and the real benchmark source (FFHQ).

authors: Lingzhi Li, Jianmin Bao, Ting Zhang, Hao Yang, Dong Chen, Fang Wen, Baining Guo
title: Face X-Ray for More General Face Forgery Detection
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2020)
intended_claim_supported: Highlights that facial blending operations leave boundary artifacts that generalize across manipulation methods.
relationship_to_proposed_method: Complementary spatial forensics reference. Emphasizes blending boundaries in swapped faces, contrasting with our whole-face synthesis focus.
